Summary (proposed targets for procurement sign-off):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) for chat (redwood-chat-13b-q4_0, streaming): p50 <= 200 ms, p95 <= 450 ms, p99 <= 850 ms
- Per-token streaming latency: p50 <= 10 ms, p95 <= 30 ms, p99 <= 80 ms (measured as time between token emission events at steady-state)
- Throughput: sustained 1200 tokens/s per GPU for short sequences (avg 80 tokens) with continuous batching; peak burst up to 2000 tokens/s
- Concurrency: 1, 8, 32 simulated user sessions; latency SLOs degrade predictably — planning to document fallbacks and recommended burst policies in the MAP

Attached for your review: optima_map_v1.xlsx (MAP with owners/dates), detailed test plan (tab), and initial synthetic results.

Subject: RE: Performance MAP: TTFT & streaming latency benchmarks for Optima POC

Hi Sam / Marta — attaching the completed benchmark pack (streaming_bench_results.csv, ttft_latency_plots.png) and a short summary here. We ran the tests on Dedicated H100 80GB (driver + runtime tuned for continuous batching). Model: redwood-chat-13b-q4_0 (production quantized profile). Test harness: 10k trials across a 150-sample prompt set representing clinical triage dialogs (40–120 tokens). Measurements taken from client-side request start to first-byte emitted (TTFT) and inter-token intervals for streaming latency. All measurements reported as p50/p95/p99.

Key results (baseline config: single request thread, model warmed, KV cache enabled):
- TTFT (ms) — redwood-chat-13b-q4_0, streaming:
  - p50: 174 ms
  - p95: 423 ms
  - p99: 812 ms

- Per-token streaming latency (ms between tokens at steady-state, 1-token granularity):
  - p50: 9.6 ms
  - p95: 27.8 ms
  - p99: 69.4 ms

- Throughput (tokens/sec per GPU, continuous streaming workload, avg prompt 80 tokens):
  - sustained: 1,250 tokens/s
  - peak burst (with batching): 2,020 tokens/s

- Concurrency behavior (observed median TTFT and p95 at different simulated concurrent sessions):
  - 1 session: TTFT p95 420 ms (matches above)
  - 8 sessions: TTFT p95 620 ms; p99 1,150 ms; moderate queuing observed when single-GPU queue grew beyond 10 active requests
  - 32 sessions: TTFT p95 1,450 ms; p99 2,650 ms; recommend dedicated pool with autoscale to maintain SLOs at this load

Notes on methodology and caveats:
- TTFT definition: client start -> first-byte out of server. We include model input tokenization and any prefix/KV cache retrieval time.
- Warm vs cold: these numbers are for warm model; cold-starts (container spin-up) are much higher and should be mitigated via reserved Dedicated capacity for production.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: non-streamed full-response latencies (end-to-end) are reported in CSV for completeness and are ~20–30% higher for long outputs due to finalization steps.
- Network variability: client-side measurements performed from a controlled GCP region; we'll provide Dockerized harness so Optima can re-run from their environment for verification.

Recommendations for MAP and close cadence:
- MAP milestones (owners/dates):
  - Redwood to provide test artifacts + raw CSV: DONE (Marissa) — 2026-02-18
  - Optima to validate with their harness and confirm acceptance criteria: Sam / Marta — target 2026-02-20
  - Legal & Procurement to receive SLA draft and performance annex: Redwood (Vivek) — target 2026-02-22
  - Final sign-off & PO: Optima — target 2026-02-26

Next steps:
1) Marta / Sam: can you confirm acceptance thresholds? Our recommended procurement thresholds that map to the above results are TTFT p95 <= 650 ms and per-token streaming p95 <= 40 ms to account for site variability.
2) I'll upload the Docker harness and a README with instructions to the shared Drive link.
3) Vivek will prepare a short SLA addendum draft and cost table for Dedicated reserved pool sizing if Optima wants consistent sub-500ms p95 at 32 concurrent sessions.

Attached: streaming_bench_results.csv (raw), ttft_latency_plots.png (plots), optima_map_v1.xlsx (MAP).

— Marissa
